lessons.title: How a lesson is organised
lessons.body:
Every YMN Learn lesson follows the same layout, so you always know where to look.

## The outline

The outline lists every lesson in the course. On a wide screen it sits beside the lesson; on a phone it folds into the Lessons button above the text. Each entry shows whether you have marked it complete.

## The lesson text

Lessons are written to be read at your own pace. Headings break the text into short sections. Nothing moves on by itself, and nothing plays sound without you choosing it.

## Below the text

- Check your understanding: a question with an explanation of the answer, when the lesson has one.
- Sources: what the lesson is based on, and when it was last revised.
- Controls to mark the lesson complete, save the course, and move to the previous or next lesson.
lessons.sources: This orientation lesson describes the YMN Learn preview itself and does not draw on external sources.

lessons.title: Finding a lesson’s sources
lessons.body:
Knowing where information comes from is part of reading it well. Each YMN Learn lesson ends with a Sources block that names what the lesson is based on.

## What the Sources block tells you

- Which publications, organisations or people the content draws on.
- When the lesson was last revised, so you can judge how current it is.
- When a lesson draws on no outside material, the block says so plainly.

## What it does not tell you

Illustrations on a lesson or course are decorative. Status labels such as In development or Completed describe the platform, not the quality of the evidence. For that, read the sources themselves.

lessons.title: Saving your place
lessons.body:
YMN Learn does not have accounts yet. Instead, this preview keeps a small record in your browser.

## Save for later

Saving a course adds it to My learning, so you can find it again. You can save courses that are still in development to follow their progress.

## Mark as complete

A lesson is only marked complete when you press the button. Scrolling to the end does not count. You can undo it at any time.

## What is stored, and where

- Only course and lesson identifiers, plus the last lesson you opened.
- Stored on this device, in this browser. It does not sync to your phone or another computer.
- Clearing your browser data, or using Clear progress in My learning, removes it.

Completing a lesson is a record for your own reference. It is not a certificate and does not indicate competence to perform any medical task.

faqs.q: Do I need to study medicine?
faqs.a: YMN is a community for youths aged 13–21 who are passionate about medicine, health and people. You do not need to study medicine. Individual opportunities may have additional requirements; check the published activity details.

faqs.q: How can I hear about activities?
faqs.a: Follow Telegram and Instagram for announcements and activity updates.
Eligibility, preparation and available places vary by activity. Follow each opportunity's published requirements.
